newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross considers using armed guards in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross considers using armed guards in Rwanda.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross said on Thursday that it was considering armed protection for its staff in Rwanda following the killing of three Spanish aid workers and an increase in violence.

Philippe Dind, head of security for the Geneva-based humanitarian agency, told a news conference that the ICRC had reduced its field presence in Rwanda following the brutal slaying of the three aid workers on Saturday night.

Dind said the use of armed guards in the field, a clear departure from ICRC's reliance on its impartiality and respect for its emblem for protection in conflict zones, was considered at a meeting of delegates in Switzerland this week.
He ruled out armed protection for ICRC staff moving in the field but said the agency wanted to hire armed guards to protect staff in their offices and residences in conflict zones.

"Rwanda certainly is a place where the idea of armed guards is being considered," he said in response to a question. He did not say what type of guards could be deployed in the tiny central African country and when.
"Today, it's not even good to be seen as an expatriate in Rwanda. That's the reason we have reduced our presence in Rwanda. Our people do not move in the field," he said.
In the past week, gunmen have killed more than 60 people in Rwanda, state radio and U.N. sources said, identifying many of the victims as survivors of the 1994 genocide.
The wave of killings was reported as the Rwandan government said it arrested three suspects, soldiers of the former hardline Hutu government, in connection with the killings of the aid workers.

The government says it suspects Hutu militiamen who returned to Rwanda from Zaire among more than 700,000 refugees last year shot dead the three aid workers from Medicos del Mundo (Doctors of the World) in the northwestern town of Ruhengeri.
Gunmen stormed a house where the aid workers were staying and demanded their passports before shooting the three Spaniards at close range. An American was shot and later had a leg amputated.
Three government soldiers guarding the compound were also killed.
